text.p: These were the main headlines from Latvia's state radio at noon on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Riga Traumatology hospital and a number of culture ministry establishments, including the State Philarmonic, have been warned that their heating supply will be cut if they don't pay their bills.

- A block of 18th century barracks in the centre of Riga is reconstructed and turned into a multi-purpose complex, housing officies and embassies, including that of the EU Commission. British Airways city office will also be situated there. The opening of Jacobs Barracks is scheduled for today.
- The building of the EU PHARE financed penstock of Jurmala sewage system commences. The EU provides 1.273 million lats and Latvia stands 314,000 lats.
- EU Commissioner Hans van den Broek finishes his two-day visit to Latvia.
